ui.title: Help
ui.no_pdf: No user manual has been stored as PDF.
ui.manual_subtitle: All help topics of the application on one page. Open the help for the current page with the question mark in the header or with F1.

general.title: General operation
general.intro: SLIM is divided into the areas “Shooting ranges” and “Data management”. The sidebar leads to the areas; the header contains language, appearance, help, main menu and user account.
general.s1: Language: choose DE, EN, FR or IT in the header. The choice is remembered.
general.s2: Appearance: switch between light and dark with the moon symbol.
general.s3: Help for the current page: question mark in the header or the F1 key.
general.s4: Main menu (three lines): user manual as PDF, online help, contact details and version of the application.
general.s5: You see the areas and shooting ranges your role is authorised for.

home.title: Entry page
home.intro: The entry page shows key figures of the shooting ranges and leads to the areas of the application.
home.s1: The tiles open the overview of the shooting ranges and the data management.
home.s2: The key figures count the shooting ranges by traffic light status; the notice about need for action opens the filtered overview.
home.s3: With the star in the sidebar you bookmark shooting ranges you need often.

areas.title: Overview of shooting ranges
areas.intro: The table shows the shooting ranges you are authorised for, with the traffic lights “Quota compliance” and “Noise exposure”.
areas.s1: Search by name or coordination section number.
areas.s2: “Need for action only” and the filters per traffic light narrow the list.
areas.s3: A click on a row opens the details; the symbols at the end of the row lead to overview, shot counts, details and simulation.
areas.s4: Traffic light: green = complied with, orange = to be checked, red = exceeded, grey = no basis, striped = cannot be assessed.
areas.s5: The thresholds and colours of the traffic lights come from the advanced configuration.

area_overview.title: Shooting range – overview
area_overview.intro: The context bar shows the selected shooting range with its two traffic lights and leads to shot counts, details and simulation.
area_overview.s1: With the selector showing number and name you switch the shooting range without leaving the area.
area_overview.s2: The content of this page (comparison with the quotas of the planning approval) is not available in this version yet.

shots.title: Shot counts
shots.intro: Here you record and manage the usages of a shooting range for one year. They are the basis of the noise calculation.
shots.s1: “Record usage”: enter firing position area, unit, date, time from/to in quarter hours, type of usage and one or more items of weapon/calibre and quantity.
shots.s2: The weapon/calibre combinations assigned to the firing position area are offered.
shots.s3: Edit and delete with the symbols at the end of the row; a deletion can be undone right afterwards.
shots.s4: Search, filters and the list of firing position areas narrow the table.
shots.s5: Usages up to and including the lock date are locked (lock symbol): they cannot be recorded, changed or deleted.

details.title: Details – receiver points
details.intro: The page shows the assessment of the noise exposure per receiver point for the chosen calculation state and period.
details.s1: Choose the calculation basis and the period at the top; if the state differs from the current one, the deviation is shown.
details.s2: A click on a receiver point of the map shows its assessment under Annex 9 and Annex 7 of the NAO with limit value, rating level and reserve.
details.s3: The colour of a point is the worst applicable assessment. Planning values apply to plant parts built after 1985.
details.s4: “List” shows the same points as a table, the worst assessment first.
details.s5: Without an imported calculation no assessment is possible; the notice leads to Data management › Calculations.

simulation.title: Simulation
simulation.intro: With the simulation you calculate the noise exposure under Annex 9 of the NAO for hypothetical shot counts. No data is changed.
simulation.s1: “Overwrite values” makes the table of yearly shot counts editable; the factors scale all values.
simulation.s2: “Run simulation” calculates the rating levels with the changed values.
simulation.s3: Map and result table show the simulated state; the actual state stays visible as a small dot next to the receiver point.

map.title: Map
map.intro: The map shows the plant parts and receiver points of a shooting range on background maps of swisstopo.
map.s1: Zoom with + and −, the mouse wheel or a double click; the house symbol restores the initial extent.
map.s2: At the bottom you find the scale bar, the scale and the coordinates of the mouse position in CH1903+ / LV95.
map.s3: Switch the background map at the bottom left; under “Layers” you show or hide plant parts and receiver points.
map.s4: “Export” creates the map extent as PDF or image, optionally with title, date, scale and further details.
map.s5: “Full view” opens the map in a new tab.

dm_areas.title: Data management – shooting ranges
dm_areas.intro: The list leads to the administration of the individual shooting ranges.
dm_areas.s1: Search by name, coordination section number and sectoral plan number; filter for active and inactive shooting ranges.
dm_areas.s2: The actions of a row open “General”, “Weapon assignment” and “Calculations” of the shooting range.
dm_areas.s3: A click on a column title sorts the table.

dm_general.title: Shooting range – general
dm_general.intro: “Overview” shows the firing position areas of the shooting range, “Master data” its core data and the quotas of the planning approval.
dm_general.s1: Master data: edit and save name, coordination section number, sectoral plan number, active status and statuses.
dm_general.s2: Quotas: record the maximum shot count per weapon/calibre. They are the target of the quota traffic light.
dm_general.s3: When leaving the page you are asked about unsaved changes.

dm_area_weapons.title: Weapon assignment
dm_area_weapons.intro: The page shows which weapon/calibre combinations are permitted in which firing position area.
dm_area_weapons.s1: Choose a firing position area; its assigned combinations are shown.
dm_area_weapons.s2: The assignment comes from the imported calculation and is displayed here, not edited.
dm_area_weapons.s3: In the shot counts the assigned combinations can be recorded.

dm_calculations.title: Calculations
dm_calculations.intro: Here you manage the immission calculations (sonARMS) of a shooting range with their calculation states.
dm_calculations.s1: Overview: deliveries and states. The pointer “current” determines the state of the assessment, the pointer “MGDM” the state for the geodata model.
dm_calculations.s2: Import: choose a calculation file and have it checked; the check notes appear before the import.
dm_calculations.s3: Level files (WLR) and operating data can be uploaded for a state.
dm_calculations.s4: Export: download calculation states and shot counts as a file.
dm_calculations.s5: Details: view the contents of a state.

dm_weapons.title: Weapons
dm_weapons.intro: Master data of the weapons: weapon/calibre combinations, weapons, calibres and weapon categories.
dm_weapons.s1: Choose a list at the top, click an entry and edit it, or record a new entry.
dm_weapons.s2: Names can be recorded in DE, FR and IT. Inactive entries are kept for existing usages.
dm_weapons.s3: An entry that is still in use cannot be deleted; its use is shown.
dm_weapons.s4: “Export” downloads the list as an Excel file.

users.title: Users, roles and apps
users.intro: The user administration grants authorisations by role.
users.s1: Record or edit users and assign them a role.
users.s2: Roles define per application area whether reading or writing is allowed.
users.s3: “Apps” shows the application areas the rights refer to.

logs.title: Logbook
logs.intro: The logbook shows sign-ins and logged changes.
logs.s2: The list can be exported as an Excel file.

system.title: Advanced configuration
system.intro: Settings that apply to the whole application. They can be changed by the application administrator role.
system.s1: Lock date: usages up to and including this date can no longer be recorded, changed or deleted.
system.s2: User manual: upload, replace or remove a PDF. It appears in the main menu.
system.s3: Thresholds planning approval: limits of the quota traffic light in percent of the target.
system.s4: Thresholds receiver points: limits of the noise traffic light as deviation from the limit value in dB.
system.s5: Traffic light colours and contact details of the main menu; “Restore defaults” resets thresholds and colours.
